proposals.title: Visible-ID color cache with projected-error validation
proposals.hypothesis: A per-selected-ID SH cache lowers moving latency without the whole-bank refresh spikes seen in P3.
proposals.mechanism: Allocate a color and last-direction entry by permanent world ID; during projection evaluate SH for first-use or direction-invalid entries and reuse others. Use projected footprint and a measured SH error bound to require tighter validity for more visible splats. Keep source SH and full-quality geometry.
proposals.interaction: Permanent IDs allow view-to-view reuse while the footprint signal prevents treating a large close-up splat like a subpixel one. The existing quality and p95 guard rejects stale color.
proposals.baseline: Current exact LOD plus visible SH; separately compare native cached SH
proposals.test: Prototype and audit on synthetic SH3, then frozen bee/shop paths with stationary, rotation, translation and LOD-change cases
proposals.primary_metric: Moving completed-frame median with cold-refresh and steady-state costs reported separately
guardrails: At most 0.5 dB loss versus current LOD
No stale ID aliasing or hidden coefficient reduction
proposals.rejection_rule: Reject if cold-refresh spikes erase gains or the error guard fails; do not extrapolate SH0 results.
failure_modes: Cache memory and random writes exceed saved SH cost
Directional error bound is too loose
proposals.cost: One new GPU cache and projection branch; requires a separate authorized experiment batch
proposals.boundary: Static SH3 scenes, one device until replicated

score_reasons.evidence_strength: P3 identifies refresh tails, not this solution's benefit.
score_reasons.expected_impact: May save visible SH without full-bank updates.
score_reasons.feasibility: Permanent IDs and projection hooks already exist.
score_reasons.information_gain: Separates cache granularity from cache validity.

proposals.title: Locality-assisted, coverage-preserving projected aggregation
proposals.hypothesis: Aggregating compatible tiny splats instead of discarding them retains aggregate opacity while reducing sort and raster work.
proposals.mechanism: Spatially order immutable banks with a permanent ID remap, bin projected tiny splats locally, and moment-merge only groups with bounded depth and color variation. Preserve summed optical contribution and depth-order constraints; leave incompatible splats unchanged. Compare locality-only, aggregation-only and combined controls.
proposals.interaction: Physical locality can reduce binning and parameter-gather cost, while depth/color constraints prevent locality from merging unrelated overlapping surfaces. This directly addresses P1's lost aggregate coverage.
prerequisites: Stable output IDs and global sorting
proposals.baseline: Exact LOD with visible SH, plus P1 contribution cutoff as a loss-control
proposals.test: Synthetic overlapping-opacity/depth-edge scenes followed by the same frozen bee, shop and city paths; retain the three ablations
proposals.primary_metric: Total moving completed-frame latency including binning and reduction
guardrails: At most 0.5 dB additional minimum foreground PSNR loss
Bijection of logical IDs after physical reordering
proposals.rejection_rule: Reject if binning/reduction costs more than the saved work or opacity/depth guard fails.
failure_modes: No compatible groups at fine depth edges
SH and internal occlusion do not merge well
Physical reordering alone changes tie order
proposals.cost: Substantial new compute path; untested and outside the completed three-proposal budget
proposals.boundary: Projected subpixel groups only; not a license to merge all distant geometry

score_reasons.evidence_strength: Cutoff failure establishes the coverage problem, not this solution.
score_reasons.expected_impact: Can reduce sort and raster while retaining coverage.
score_reasons.feasibility: WebGPU reductions exist but depth-safe grouping is nontrivial.
score_reasons.testability: Three explicit ablations and synthetic opacity controls.
score_reasons.information_gain: Distinguishes locality cost from aggregation quality.
score_reasons.generality: SH0 and SH3, subject to compatibility.
score_reasons.novelty: New projected aggregation operator and bank layout.
score_reasons.cost_efficiency: Extra passes could erase all gains.

rejections.reason: Physical bank order and directional cache invalidation have no direct causal interaction without a cache operator. Test locality alone as an ablation in P5 rather than invent a combined win.
Footprint plus depth/color constraints and visible SH identifies eligible groups but supplies no reduction operator. The complete aggregation operator is covered by P5.
Aggregate coverage does not determine directional SH-cache validity. Coupling the signals could reuse stale color.
Depth/color constraints and existing visible SH plus a quality guard are not a new acceleration operator.
